pointers.sentence: Cache headers and conditional requests: `django/utils/cache.py`

`django/utils/cache.py` holds the functions that tell browsers and proxies whether and for how long to keep a response, `patch_cache_control`, `patch_response_headers`, `add_never_cache_headers` and `patch_vary_headers`, and `get_conditional_response`, which decides from a request's preconditions whether to answer 304 Not Modified or 412 Precondition Failed instead.

On the way out only `True` itself gives the bare name; any other value gives the name, `=` and the value as text, so `private=False` writes `private=False` (`django/utils/cache.py:patch_cache_control`).
`get_max_age` reads `"max-age"` back as an integer, or `None` when it is missing or not a whole number (`django/utils/cache.py:get_max_age`).

It sets `"Expires"` that many seconds from now, written by `http_date`, unless the response has one, and passes the lifetime to `patch_cache_control` as the max-age (`django/utils/cache.py:patch_response_headers`).

`add_never_cache_headers` calls it with -1, which sets `"Expires"`, where there is none, to the present moment and `"max-age"` to 0, then adds `"no-cache"`, `"no-store"`, `"must-revalidate"` and `"private"`, the last removing any `"public"` (`django/utils/cache.py:add_never_cache_headers`).
If `"*"` is among the names, old or new, the header becomes `"*"` alone (`django/utils/cache.py:patch_vary_headers`).
`has_vary_header` asks whether a name is there, on the same terms (`django/utils/cache.py:has_vary_header`).
It returns a 304 or a 412 to send instead, or else the response it was given, `None` if none (`django/utils/cache.py:get_conditional_response`).
If-Match uses the strong comparison: the current tag must be in the list exactly, so a weak one never matches, though `"*"` matches any tag (`django/utils/cache.py:_if_match_passes`).
If-None-Match uses the weak comparison, stripping `"W/"` from both sides first (`django/utils/cache.py:_if_none_match_passes`).

The dates are compared as integers, and with no last-modified time If-Modified-Since never gives a 304 (`django/utils/cache.py:_if_modified_since_passes`), while If-Unmodified-Since, unless an If-Match came with it, always gives a 412, to a `"GET"` as well (`django/utils/cache.py:_if_unmodified_since_passes`).

The dates are compared as integers, and with no last-modified time If-Modified-Since never gives a 304 (`django/utils/cache.py:_if_modified_since_passes`), while If-Unmodified-Since, unless an If-Match came with it, always gives a 412, to a `"GET"` as well (`django/utils/cache.py:_if_unmodified_since_passes`).

Given the full response, it copies over Cache-Control, Content-Location, `"Date"`, `"ETag"`, `"Expires"`, Last-Modified and `"Vary"`, the headers RFC 9110's section 15.4.5 requires and Last-Modified, as its comment says, and the cookies, which by the old cookie specification its comment quotes a proxy passes on with a 304 as with a 200 (`django/utils/cache.py:_not_modified`).
`_precondition_failed` makes the 412, an `HttpResponse` with an empty body, and logs it through `log_response` as a warning to `"django.request"` (`django/utils/cache.py:_precondition_failed`).
`ConditionalGetMiddleware`'s one hook is `process_response`, so it acts on the finished response, after the view has run (`django/middleware/http.py:ConditionalGetMiddleware.process_response`).

Unless Cache-Control holds `"no-store"`, which `ConditionalGetMiddleware.needs_etag` looks for, a response without an `"ETag"` is given one by `set_response_etag`: the MD5 of the content in quotes, a strong tag, and none for a streaming or an empty response (`django/utils/cache.py:set_response_etag`).
The middleware saves sending the body, not making it, the comparison the documentation draws with `condition` (`docs/topics/conditional-view-processing.txt`).

The `condition` decorator calls `get_conditional_response` before the view, with what its functions return: the tag through `quote_etag`, so a bare one becomes strong, and the time, made aware in UTC if naive, in whole seconds (`django/views/decorators/http.py:condition`).

So, as the documentation says, a decorator that sets `"Vary"` or Cache-Control must stand above `condition` for its headers to reach a 304 ([View decorators](../views/decorators.md)) (`docs/topics/conditional-view-processing.txt`).
